answer: Finite terrain survey proofs.** Each identity anchor is a fresh, non-reusable observation of a physical site — a tundra plot, a nadir depth reading, or similar — recorded with sensor noise and timestamp, then checked against a global database that retires every submitted sample. Duplicating an identity requires re-surveying new ground at attacker cost: one field trip and instrument set per sybil. Costs scale with terrain scarcity, not stake.
